title: Reaction-diffusion of morphogens accounts for biological pattern

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Reaction-diffusion of morphogens accounts for biological pattern

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Chemical substances that react and diffuse through tissue (morphogens) are sufficient to account for the main phenomena of morphogenesis.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: no canonical formalization: the claim asserts that a biological pattern is generated by a system of the form u_t = F(u) + D\nabla^2 u with D not proportional to the identity

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: Alan Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Context in the nanopub
fields.value: Formal status: a framework rather than a mathematical proposition. Kondo and Asai (1995) confirmed the predicted stripe-branching dynamics in Pomacanthus and Castets et al. (1990) produced Turing patterns chemically. Mechanical buckling, prepatterns and cell-cell signalling can produce the same patterns, so a matching pattern alone does not identify the mechanism.
